bandReport.notes: All 4 pages opened and read from the column crops (c1 then c2); itemsByPage filled page by page as I went, no page empty. Numbers 46-60 contiguous, no skips. Page 11 carries only 3 items because items 51 and 52 are long and 52 straddles the gutter. COMPLETENESS: item 46 is whole on p10-c1 (stem + four numbered statements + question line + all four options); I also hold band b2 and can confirm directly that p9-c2 ends with item 45 complete above the '[ P.T.O.' rule, so the b2/b3 seam at 45/46 is clean with no item straddling it. Item 60 is whole on p13-c2 (stem + lead-in + two numbered statements + question line + all four options) and p13-c2 ends with the '[ P.T.O.' rule below it. TERRITORY I DO NOT OWN: I opened p14-c1 for structure only (pages 14-21 belong to another agent) and it opens cleanly at item 61 with its own number and full option block, so the 60/61 seam is clean and nothing of item 60 runs onto p14. I transcribed nothing from p14. TWO ITEMS SPAN THE GUTTER on these pages, and both are genuine mid-item column breaks rather than sliced crops. Item 52: its stem and its option (a) fill the bottom of p11-c1, and options (b), (c), (d) sit at the TOP of p11-c2 with no item number above them. Item 55: its stem and its numbered statement 1 end p12-c1, and statements 2 and 3, the question line and all four options continue at the top of p12-c2. In both cases reading order c1-then-c2 attributes the continuation correctly, and for item 52 I confirmed the layout against p11.png (structure only) before transcribing, because an unnumbered option block at the head of c2 is exactly the shape that produces options attributed to the neighbouring question. Item 53 begins below 52's option block and has its own four options; item 56 likewise below 55's. CROPS: no sliced crop on any of pages 10-13; every c2 carries only a thin sliver of c1's line-END letters down its left edge (expected two-column overlap), and where c2 opens with an item number it is intact (48, 54, 59). p12-c1 and p13-c1 both carry a heavy black BINDING-SHADOW artifact down their left margin from the original scan - it lies entirely outside the text block and obscures no question text; I checked both against p12.png/p13.png and every line is fully legible. p11-c1 clips the leading digit of the page number '23' in its bottom-right corner - footer only, no question text affected. PRINTED FORM: no pair grids or pipe tables on these pages, no bold or italic emphasis, no mathematical notation. Items 58 and 60 have an unusual two-part stem - 'Consider the following statements :' followed by a separate lead-in sentence ('The Environment Protection Act, 1986 empowers the Government of India to' / 'As per the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Central (Amendment) Rules, 2018') and only then the numbered statements, whose items read as continuations of that lead-in rather than as free-standing sentences. Transcribed in that printed order and kept on their own lines, since collapsing the lead-in into the numbered items would change what each statement asserts. Item 46 option (a) is printed '1 and 2' and (d) '1, 3 and 4' WITHOUT the word 'only' while (c) carries it; item 51's options are all printed without 'only' - transcribed verbatim as printed, the inconsistency is the booklet's, not mine. No printed defect, no duplicated option text, no unreadable item on these pages. SUBTOPICS: one soft label not in catalog.json - item 60 'Labour Laws and Industrial Relations' (Economy > Employment, Poverty and Social Development). The item is about the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Rules, i.e. labour LEGISLATION, and the chapter's nearest listed subtopic 'Employment and Labour Statistics' is about statistics, which this is not; no other chapter in the catalog covers labour law. Every other subject/chapter/subtopic is copied verbatim from catalog.json.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements :
1. The motion to impeach a Judge of the Supreme Court of India cannot be rejected by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha as per the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968.
2. The Constitution of India defines and gives details of what constitutes 'incapacity and proved misbehaviour' of the Judges of the Supreme Court of India.
3. The details of the process of impeachment of the Judges of the Supreme Court of India are given in the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968.
4. If the motion for the impeachment of a Judge is taken up for voting, the law requires the motion to be backed by each House of the Parliament and supported by a majority of total membership of that House and by not less than two-thirds of total members of that House present and voting.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
